test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Evaluate the following statements related to reusable launch vehicles (RLVS):

Statement 1: RLVs are being explored primarily to enhance launch efficiency and reduce the recurring cost of satellite deployment.

Statement 2: The development of RLVs increases operational complexity, making them less viable compared to traditional expendablı systems.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reusable Launch Vehicles (RLVs)** are engineered with the specific goal of recovering the **launch vehicle stages** for multiple missions. This approach drastically lowers the **recurring costs** associated with space flight, as the most expensive components, such as **cryogenic engines** and **advanced avionics**, are not discarded after a single use. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• While **RLVs** involve significantly higher **operational complexity** due to the requirement for **re-entry heat shielding**, **retro-propulsion**, and **autonomous landing systems**, this does not make them less viable. On the contrary, the ability to refurbish and relaunch makes them **highly viable** for the modern **commercial space industry**, where high **launch frequency** and cost-efficiency are paramount. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ISRO RLV-TD**: The **Indian Space Research Organisation** is developing the **Reusable Launch Vehicle-Technology Demonstrator (RLV-TD)** to achieve a **Two-Stage-to-Orbit (TSTO)** fully reusable vehicle.
 
 
• **RLV-LEX**: ISRO successfully conducted the **Autonomous Landing Mission** at **Chitradurga, Karnataka**, demonstrating **unmanned landing** capabilities under conditions similar to a return from space.
 
• **Economic Goals**: These technologies aim to reduce the cost of **payload delivery** to **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** to about 1/10th of current costs.
 
 
 
• **Expendable Launch Vehicles (ELVs)**:
 
 
• Traditional systems like the **PSLV** or **GSLV** are **expendable**, meaning the boosters are lost in the **ocean** after fuel exhaustion.
 
• While **ELVs** have simpler designs, they require **new hardware manufacturing** for every single mission, leading to massive financial waste.
